# Synthetic resume fixtures

Small, deterministic PDF fixtures for the extraction pipeline (REQ-FR-012,
batches 2.2-2.3). None of them contains a real resume or any real person's
details — they are hand-written PDF objects (a Helvetica font, a `612x792`
MediaBox and a correct xref table), generated by a throwaway script and then
committed so the tests never generate bytes at run time.

| File | What it exercises |
|---|---|
| `simple_text.pdf` | A normal, text-bearing PDF (2 pages). |
| `scanned_no_text.pdf` | A valid PDF whose page extracts to no text (a scan with no text layer). |
| `three_pages.pdf` | Three pages, for the page-limit check. |
| `truncated.pdf` | Half of a valid PDF — malformed. |
| `encrypted.pdf` | A valid trailer carrying an `/Encrypt` dict with a bogus `O`/`U`; pdfminer fails authentication and raises `PDFPasswordIncorrect`. |
| `empty.pdf` | Zero bytes. |
| `unsupported.docx` | A DOCX signature (`PK\x03\x04`) — the wrong-magic-bytes case, not a real document. |

The `encrypted.pdf` fixture is a password-protection *signal*, not a real
encrypted document: pdfminer attempts authentication with the empty password,
fails, and raises before any stream is parsed, which is exactly what the
extractor turns into the `password_protected` code. No encryption key is
materialised anywhere.
